text.p: H.J. Heinz Co Chairman Tony O'Reilly said Friday acquisitions would be "very important" for his company in the coming months, adding acquisitions in Eastern Europe and Southeast Asia would soon be announced.

While declining to be specific, O'Reilly told Reuters in a bried interview, "I can say at the moment that there is a real potential for acquisitions in Eastern Europe, and a very good one in Southeast Asia."
O'Reilly made his comments to Reuters following a meeting for analysts in San Francisco that detailed the company's expected reorganization.

The reorganization is designed to focus Heinz on its six core units and shed ancillary businesses. O'Reilly said the reconfigured company expects to realize over $2 billion in free cash flow over the next five years, with $1 billion in the next 12 months.
When asked by Reuters how much of the projected cash flow would be spent on acquisitions, O'Reilly said, "I can't say at this stage.
"I would say that within the next two to three months you will expect an announcement" on Eastern European and Southeast Asian acquisitions.
